scope.universe: Total decision languages; every input must satisfy the verifier/sampler gap.

QMA2.definition: A polynomial-time uniform polynomial-size H,T,X,CNOT verifier with two separately normalized, polynomial-length pure quantum witnesses. Completeness2/3 and soundness1/3 hold on every input, with soundness quantified over every product pair.
trusted_bridges: Pure product witnesses suffice for arbitrary separable mixtures by linearity/convexity.
The fixed universal gate set and constant gap agree with the usual bounded-error model.
Harrow–Montanaro supplies gap amplification and equivalence with polynomially many unentangled witnesses.
pitfalls: A single arbitrary joint witness would define QMA, not QMA2.
State quantification is part of witness semantics, not uncomputable advice available to the verifier.
The promise-complete problems are not silently added to the total-language universe.

StoqMA.definition: A concrete polynomial-time uniform NOT/CNOT/Toffoli circuit receives input, a quantum witness, zero ancillas and plus ancillas, then measures one output in the X basis. Union over FP rational length-dependent1/2≤b<a≤1 with an explicit inverse-polynomial gap.
trusted_bridges: Explicit unary circuit serialization has polynomial overhead.
The rational threshold union is the endpoint intended by unparameterized StoqMA here; no all-threshold equivalence theorem is assumed.
pitfalls: Fixed2/3 versus1/3 is incompatible with the stoquastic soundness floor.
The exact b=1/2 boundary has an NP characterization and is not the whole threshold union.
Completeness amplification toward1 is an open problem in the general model.

BQL.definition: On actual input x, a concrete deterministic transducer with simultaneous logarithmic work space and polynomial running time emits a polynomial-size circuit C_x on O(log|x|) qubits. The qubits start at zero, and every input has gap2/3 versus1/3.
trusted_bridges: Definitions4–5 of Fefferman–Remscrim directly use input-dependent DSPACE(s)-uniform circuits over H,CNOT,T with all-zero initial state; Theorem1 identifies them with the intermediate-measurement model.
Classical input access belongs to the bounded classical controller; the entire n-bit input is not copied into counted quantum workspace.
pitfalls: Without polynomial time the class equals PL, a different endpoint.
A polynomial-time rather than logspace circuit generator would accidentally supply P-level preprocessing.
StrongFewL is not UL; an all-pairs fewness hypothesis cannot be dropped.

QSZK.definition: Two concrete polynomial-time quantum samplers produce mixed states by discarding explicit environment registers. On every yes input their output trace distance is≥2/3; on every no input it is≤1/3. The implementation uses the variational maximum over projective binary measurements.
trusted_bridges: The finite-dimensional variational projective-measurement formula equals half the trace norm by the Helstrom theorem.
QSD completeness, polarization and honest-verifier/full-QSZK equivalence identify this total reduction class with interactive QSZK.
Weak endpoints are harmless:1/3<3/8<(5/8)^2<2/3 with the middle inequality3/8<25/64; polarization provides arbitrary slack for the reverse encoding.
pitfalls: The mathematical measurement in the distance definition is unrestricted; it is not an efficient oracle given to a sampler.
Measurements access only retained output qubits, never discarded environment.
Different normalizations of trace distance require the factor1/2.
Interchanging the two samplers leaves distance unchanged and does not establish complement closure.

facts.justification: Ignore the second witness register. A zero-qubit normalized second witness suffices; the first verifier and its gap are unchanged.

Guess exponentially many polynomial-precision amplitudes for the two polynomial-qubit witnesses and simulate the polynomial-size verifier to constant additive accuracy. The constant gap permits normalization and rounding; nondeterministic exponential time suffices.

Use an amplified perfectly complete coherent MA verifier and an output-controlled swap of zero and plus ancillas. The X-measurement acceptance is1 on yes witnesses and at most1/2+negligible on no inputs, an allowed threshold pair in the union.
Apply the stoquastic-verifier SBP simulation to each efficiently computable inverse-polynomial-gap threshold pair. No amplification to a single fixed threshold pair is assumed.
A general quantum verifier can implement zero/plus preparation, the reversible circuit, and final X measurement. QMA amplification handles the efficiently known inverse-polynomial acceptance gap.

An amplified BQP algorithm yields a classical output bit distribution with mass near1 on yes and near0 on no. Compare this distribution with a fixed zero bit, retaining the result and discarding work; the trace distance has the QSD gap on every input.

Use the complete Statistical Difference characterization of SZK, generate diagonal quantum output states coherently, and discard the randomness. Their trace distance equals classical total variation distance. The full-QSZK completeness bridge then applies.
QSZK⊆QIP(2)⊆PSPACE, restricted to inputs forming a total language.
Use the standard polynomial-time, logarithmic-space quantum simulation of fair-coin computation and space-preserving measurement elimination.
The §2.3 chain explicitly places polynomial-time bounded-error quantum logspace in PL; the benchmark retains that polynomial time bound.

rules.justification: QMA⊆PP and complement closure of PP give QMA=PP=coQMA. Theorem4 gives P^PP⊆QMA; hence PSharpP⊆PP. Equivalently use Theorem2, PH^PP=QMA. No CH collapse is asserted.
Complementing the premise gives the reverse containment. Theorem11 then gives PH^QMA=QMA and therefore PH⊆QMA. Theorem3 states the weaker resulting PH⊆PP.

family_reviews.reviewed_orientations: both; duplicates with two focus endpoints appear only once in incident_pairs
family_reviews.notes: QSZK and QMA2 are not put in PP, PSharpP or CH by a shared PSPACE/NEXP upper bound. StoqMA reaches PP via SBP; BQL reaches P via PL. Exact-counting and postselection characterizations remain distinct.

family_reviews.reviewed_orientations: both; duplicates with two focus endpoints appear only once in incident_pairs
family_reviews.notes: P and NP enter QMA2/StoqMA by existing QMA/MA paths; BQL⊆P follows from PL. NPcapcoNP is not identified with UPcapcoUP or a quantum witness class.

family_reviews.reviewed_orientations: both; duplicates with two focus endpoints appear only once in incident_pairs
family_reviews.notes: QMA2⊆NEXP; QSZK⊆PSPACE; BQL and StoqMA inherit smaller upper bounds. Baseline hierarchy negatives and regular-padding consequences propagate; no independent new ordinary quantum separation is proposed.

family_reviews.reviewed_orientations: both; duplicates with two focus endpoints appear only once in incident_pairs
family_reviews.notes: No general PH containment of QSZK or QMA2 is inferred. StoqMA enters PH through AM. New QMA complement-collapse rule is conditional and does not assert QMA complement closure.

family_reviews.reviewed_orientations: both; duplicates with two focus endpoints appear only once in incident_pairs
family_reviews.notes: SZK transfers through complete classical Statistical Difference, not an unsupported assertion about quantum security of every classical protocol. MA⊆StoqMA⊆SBP⊆AM. QSZK/QMA and QSZK/QMA2 remain unresolved where closure does not decide them.

family_reviews.reviewed_orientations: both; duplicates with two focus endpoints appear only once in incident_pairs
family_reviews.notes: QMA2 uses product witnesses; StoqMA has restricted gates and threshold union; QSZK has two samplers and output-only distance; BQL has simultaneous polynomial-time/logspace control. No oracle or restricted-amplitude result is an ordinary separation.

family_reviews.reviewed_orientations: both; duplicates with two focus endpoints appear only once in incident_pairs
family_reviews.notes: BPL⊆BQL, BPP⊆BQP⊆QSZK and MA⊆StoqMA supply the ordinary paths. No BQL⊆BPL or BQP⊆StoqMA simulation is inferred.

family_reviews.reviewed_orientations: both; duplicates with two focus endpoints appear only once in incident_pairs
family_reviews.notes: ExistsR is binary-language ETR reducibility. Real-valued PCP symbols and nonlinear witness optimization do not yield a finite-qubit verifier or quantum class containment.

family_reviews.reviewed_orientations: both; duplicates with two focus endpoints appear only once in incident_pairs

rejected_transfers.reason: Apers–Edenhofer proves StrongFewL⊆BQL; ordinary UL can have many paths to rejecting/intermediate configurations.
All-pairs or endpoint path-count promises are required. Checking strong fewness gives one total language, not all directed reachability.
This equality is known for postselection or unrestricted-time BQL, not the polynomial-time model.
BQL⊆PL⊆NC does not imply SC; simultaneous resource bounds require a separate algorithm.
The generic upper bound is NEXP. A quantum polynomial hierarchy and special verifier families cannot be identified with the classical counting hierarchy.
The2026 EXP upper bound applies to restricted StoqMA(2), not unrestricted product-witness QMA(2).
The exact b=1/2 boundary equals NP; the roster uses the entire admissible inverse-polynomial-gap threshold union.
Error reduction would imply this, but that error reduction remains a conjecture.
A space-efficient honest prover still participates in a two-message interactive protocol. No corresponding single-message or PP upper bound is proved.
Different separability testing problems are complete for these classes; their distinct norms/promises do not yield a reduction between them.

Classical adaptive PP queries collapse under the premise; replacing outer PP by QMA under arbitrary oracles is not justified. Yirka2025 repaired the separate, stronger quantum-advice theorem, so that result is not described as open at the cutoff.

recent_triage.finding: No additional ordinary incident-pair seed identified. Claimed post-cutoff results are not part of the baseline and were not validated here.

Candidate_unknown means this audit did not locate a qualifying theorem, not independence or a proof of historical openness.
Model-to-literature correspondences are trusted, explicit bridges; the new sanity theorems do not formalize completeness, amplification or space-preserving simulation.
No quantitative residual-error estimate is inferred solely from this bounded extension review. Independent adversarial review of the new definitions remains required.
